 5 car accident law firms in Onondaga County to compare before hiring
 After a crash in Syracuse, the hardest part of hiring a lawyer is often getting to one. Injuries limit travel, insurers call within days, and New York changed its car accident rules in May 2026. This guide compares five Syracuse-area firms that list car accident claims as a practice area, using what each firm publishes about consultations, office locations, fees, and case expenses. It also explains the 2026 law changes every Onondaga County driver should understand before signing a retainer.
 This is general information, not legal advice.
 Key Takeaways 
 Two of the five firms say they will come to clients who cannot travel, which matters most when recovery keeps you at home or in the hospital.
 All five advertise a free consultation, and four state that attorney fees depend on a recovery.
 Only one firm publishes a typical fee percentage, so ask every firm for its percentage in writing.
 For lawsuits started on or after May 26, 2026, a driver found more at fault than the other side can be barred from recovery, and the 90/180-day serious injury category no longer applies.
 Your no-fault application is generally due to your insurer within 30 days of the crash.
 What Changed in New York Car Accident Law in 2026 
 On May 26, 2026, New York amended Insurance Law Section 5102(d), Section 5104 and CPLR 1411 as part of the state budget. The changes apply to actions commenced on or after that date.
 Three changes matter most for crash victims:
 The 90/180-day category is gone. A temporary injury that kept you from your usual activities for 90 of the first 180 days no longer qualifies as a “serious injury” on its own. Claims for pain and suffering now need to fit one of the remaining categories, such as a fracture, significant disfigurement, or a permanent or significant limitation.
 A new fault bar for motor vehicle cases. Under new CPLR 1411(b), a claimant whose fault is greater than the fault of the defendant, or of the defendants combined, can be barred from recovery. Most other injury claims still follow pure comparative negligence.
 Fault is decided first. The trier of fact now decides fault before deciding whether an injury is serious.
 The no-fault basics did not change, though they rarely cover every cost that follows a car accident , such as vehicle repairs. Every New York auto policy provides up to $50,000 in basic economic loss coverage for medical bills and lost earnings, regardless of who caused the crash. The written no-fault application (Form NF-2) is generally due within 30 days of the accident, and most injury lawsuits must be filed within three years.
 Because some firm websites still describe the older rules, ask any lawyer you consult how the 2026 changes affect your specific claim.
 How Common Are Crashes in Onondaga County? 
 New York State DMV crash records published on data.ny.gov show Onondaga County logged 10,845 reported crashes in 2024, including 3,301 in the City of Syracuse. The county recorded 32 fatal crashes that year, and 46,596 reported crashes across 2021 through 2024.
 How We Picked 
 We reviewed each firm’s own website, including its car accident, contact and fee pages, as of October 31, 2026. Firms had to list car or auto accident claims as a practice area and keep an office in Syracuse or nearby in Onondaga County. We then compared consultation access, office location, published fee terms, and how each firm handles case expenses.
 This is an editorial comparison, not a certification. We did not hire these firms or assess case outcomes.
 Side-by-Side Comparison 
 Firm Syracuse-area office Best for Consultation access Published fee terms 
 Stanley Law Offices 215 Burnet Ave, Syracuse Clients who cannot travel Free; home and hospital visits No fee unless they win; case expenses advanced 
 DeFrancisco & Falgiatano, LLP 6739 Myers Rd, East Syracuse Readers across Upstate NY Free; line answered 24/7; will travel to clients No attorney fee unless compensation is recovered 
 Bottar Law, PLLC 7078 E Genesee St, Fayetteville Severe and catastrophic injuries Free consultation Ask for written terms 
 Catalano Law Burnet Ave, Syracuse Upfront fee transparency Free, no-obligation review Typically one-third; no fee unless they win 
 William Mattar 300 S State St, Syracuse Motor-vehicle-only focus Free case reviews; phones answered 24/7 No fee until they win 
 1. Stanley Law Offices 
 Founded in 1982 by Syracuse native Joe Stanley, the firm has spent more than four decades representing injured families across Upstate New York. It runs its main office on Burnet Avenue and serves Onondaga County communities including Cicero, Clay, Manlius, DeWitt, Camillus, Liverpool and Baldwinsville. For injured readers who cannot make an office visit, Stanley Law Offices offers consultations at home, in the hospital or by video, so the first meeting can happen wherever you are recovering.
 Pros 
 Consultations at home, in the hospital or by video for clients who cannot travel
 $0 upfront, with all case expenses advanced by the firm
 Joe Stanley is Board Certified in Civil Trial Practice and has been named to Super Lawyers every year since 2008
 Cons 
 No fee percentage published on its Syracuse car accident page
 Multiple offices across Upstate New York and Pennsylvania, so confirm who will handle your file
 Why we picked it 
 Access ranked it first. The firm describes its approach as no-nonsense, taking over insurer communication and moving quickly to preserve evidence such as surveillance footage, dashcam video and vehicle data. Its site reports a 4.7 rating across more than 900 verified reviews, and Spanish-speaking clients are served.
 Fees 
 The firm works on contingency, so you pay nothing unless it wins, and it advances case expenses. Ask for the percentage and how advanced expenses are repaid from a recovery.
 2. DeFrancisco & Falgiatano, LLP 
 The firm’s principal office is at 6739 Myers Rd in East Syracuse, with appointment-only offices in Oneida, Watertown, New Hartford, Binghamton, Cortland, Rochester, Oswego, Albany, Buffalo and Scranton, Pennsylvania. Its practice covers car, truck and motorcycle accidents alongside medical malpractice and birth injuries.
 Pros 
 Free consultations, available 24/7
 States it will travel to clients
 Wide network of appointment-only offices
 Cons 
 Principal office is in East Syracuse, not downtown
 Its car accident page still describes pre-2026 fault and serious injury rules
 Why we picked it 
 It suits readers who live outside Syracuse or want an attorney to come to them. Since the practice also covers malpractice, ask how much of the team’s caseload involves car crashes.
 Fees 
 The firm states consultations are free and no attorney fees are owed unless compensation is recovered. Request the percentage and expense terms in writing.
 3. Bottar Law, PLLC 
 Founded in 1983, Bottar Law is based at the Fairfield Estate, 7078 E Genesee St in Fayetteville, with an Albany office by appointment only. It lists car and automobile accidents among its practice areas, along with catastrophic injuries such as amputation, blindness, burns and disfiguring scarring.
 Pros 
 Car and automobile accident claims listed as a practice area
 Dedicated catastrophic injury practice
 Free consultation
 Cons 
 Office is in Fayetteville rather than Syracuse proper
 No fee percentage published on the pages we reviewed
 Why we picked it 
 It fits readers with severe injuries who want a firm built around high-stakes injury cases. The firm says every claim it accepts is actively researched and aggressively pursued, so ask early whether your case fits its practice.
 Fees 
 Consultations are free. Ask for the contingency percentage and expense terms before signing.
 4. Catalano Law 
 Catalano Law keeps a Syracuse office on Burnet Avenue and handles car, truck and motorcycle accident claims. Its published results include a $2.3 million car accident settlement.
 Pros 
 Publishes a typical fee percentage
 “No Fee Guarantee” means no fee unless it wins
 Free, no-obligation case review
 Cons 
 A typical percentage is not a quote for your case
 Founder Peter Catalano previously practiced at Alexander & Catalano, so older directory listings may show that name
 Why we picked it 
 It is the clearest starting point for readers who want fee numbers before the first call. The firm also covers slip-and-fall and work injury claims.
 Fees 
 The firm uses a contingency contract approved by the New York State Bar Association, with a fixed percentage that is typically one-third. Its truck accident page says no fee or expenses are owed without a recovery, so confirm the same applies to car cases.
 5. William Mattar 
 William Mattar’s Syracuse office is at One Park Place, 300 S. State St., Suite 130, with its principal office in Williamsville and other offices in Buffalo, Rochester, Albany and Long Island. The firm describes itself as New York’s largest motor vehicle accident firm, with more than 30 years representing injured people.
 Pros 
 Motor vehicle accident focus, including car, truck, motorcycle and rideshare claims
 Phones answered 24/7
 Free case reviews
 Cons 
 Statewide firm, so confirm which attorney handles your file locally
 No fee percentage published on the pages we reviewed
 Why we picked it 
 It suits readers who want a firm focused on vehicle crashes rather than a general injury practice. Its Syracuse car accident page covers no-fault benefits, the serious injury threshold and liability claims in Onondaga County.
 Fees 
 The firm advertises “No Fee Until We Win.” Ask for the percentage and how costs are handled if there is no recovery.
 Conclusion 
 The right Syracuse car accident lawyer depends on your situation. If injuries keep you at home or in the hospital, start with firms that come to you. If cost is the first question, start with a firm that publishes its percentage. For severe injuries, ask about catastrophic injury experience early.
 Whichever firm you call, file your no-fault application within 30 days, ask how the 2026 fault and serious injury changes affect your claim, and get the fee percentage, expense terms and termination terms in writing before you sign.
 FAQ 
 How much does a car accident lawyer in Syracuse cost? Most work on contingency, so attorney fees come out of a recovery. One firm in this guide publishes a typical rate of one-third. Always ask who pays case expenses if you lose.
 How soon do I need to file a no-fault claim in New York? The written no-fault application is generally due within 30 days of the accident. Late filing can cost you benefits.
 How long do I have to sue after a car accident in New York? Most personal injury lawsuits must be filed within three years. Claims involving government vehicles have much shorter notice deadlines.
 Can I still recover if I was partly at fault? For lawsuits started on or after May 26, 2026, a claimant found more at fault than the other side can be barred from recovery. If your share is smaller, damages are generally reduced by your percentage of fault.
 Can a lawyer meet me at home or in the hospital? Yes. Some Syracuse firms offer home and hospital visits. Ask about this when you first call.
